---
title: "On macOS and Windows, two files that differ only by case overwrite each other"
ref: ENV-06
categories: [OS and CI]
impact: silencieux
attendu: "two separate files, `Results.csv` and `results.csv`"
versions: "All, on a case-insensitive file system"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2021)"
---

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
write.csv(raw, file = "output/Results.csv")
write.csv(clean, file = "output/results.csv")
list.files("output")
```

```text
[1] "Results.csv"
```
:::

This pitfall depends on the machine's file system, so it cannot be replayed in the browser.

## Why

By default, macOS and Windows drives ignore case: `Results.csv` and `results.csv` refer to the same file. The second `write.csv()` therefore overwrites the first, without an error, and the file keeps the name it was first created with.

On Linux, in CI or on a server, both files coexist. The same script produces a different result depending on the machine, and a git repository that contains both names can no longer be checked out cleanly on a Mac.

## The fix

Pick a naming convention (all lowercase, for example) and never have two names that differ only by case.

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
write.csv(raw, file = "output/results_raw.csv")
write.csv(clean, file = "output/results_clean.csv")
```
:::
